summary: Remote-controlled shell PTY and filesystem operations over WebSocket
details: The package's main entry connects to a WebSocket server (default loopback, but documented usage is `--server wss://<remote>`) and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote party full control of the installer's host. `terminal_create` spawns a bash/pwsh PTY and `terminal_input` writes network-sourced bytes directly into the PTY; additional handlers implement arbitrary `read_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, and `git_*` operations. Whoever controls the configured WebSocket endpoint therefore has RCE and arbitrary filesystem access on the installer's machine. index.js additionally has heavy top-level side effects when required: it runs `npm install` in the package directory if `node_modules` is missing, clones or `git pull --ff-only`s `https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git` from the unpinned mutable `main` branch into `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`, mutates `~/.claude/settings.json`, `known_marketplaces.json`, and `installed_plugins.json`, and calls `connect()` at import time. The git source matches the publisher's own repo but is unpinned, so future commits to that branch execute on every startup.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
